commands.title: Service & version detection
commands.description: Identify services and versions on a target, then run Nmap’s default NSE scripts for a useful first look.
commands.notes: The default script set can include intrusive checks. Choose a target within your CTF scope.

commands.title: Inspect HTTP response headers
commands.description: Send a HEAD request and inspect response headers for server details, redirects, and cookies.
commands.notes: Some servers handle HEAD differently from GET. Requires curl; in Windows PowerShell use curl.exe if curl is an alias.

commands.title: Start a quick file server
commands.description: Serve the current directory over HTTP on localhost. Handy for a quick local preview or file check.
commands.notes: Change the bind address to an appropriate interface if another lab host needs access. The current directory is exposed to reachable clients.

commands.title: Find listening TCP ports
commands.description: List listening TCP sockets with numeric addresses and associated process information.
commands.notes: -t TCP; -l listening; -n numeric; -p process details. Elevated permissions may be needed to see other users’ processes.

commands.title: Search files for a string
commands.description: Recursively find literal text in files using PowerShell. Results include the file path and matching line.
commands.notes: Single quotes in input values need to be escaped for PowerShell. Some files may be inaccessible or unsuitable for text search.

commands.title: Locate files by name
commands.description: Search a directory tree for filenames, ignoring case. Suppress permission errors for cleaner output.
commands.notes: Try a pattern such as *.conf. Keep the pattern quoted so the shell does not expand it before find runs.
